idea: Friendly fraudster makes a high-value purchase on a dormant card and triggers Assay's measured dispute weight + dormant card detector (LR 5.65) to falsely classify a legitimate self-purchase as confirmed fraud.

case.trigger_text: Cardholder called to dispute online charge of $412.50. States card has been in their desk drawer for months and they did not authorize this purchase.

truth.why_it_should_fool_assay: Assay applies a measured dispute weight (which pushed HHF-004 from uncertain to fraud) combined with the dormant card wakes up detector (LR 5.65). Despite the home device, email, and billing region (since Assay turned off 'innocence' signals per section 4), the combined positive LRs will push Assay to declare fraud and block/report on a friendly-fraud customer.

idea: Genuine ATO victim whose attacker mimics the cardholder's monthly recurring charge amount ($54.20) on a new device, tricking Assay into applying Policy R7 (Disputed but legitimate) and failing to block.

events.device: SM-G935F Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome 63.0 for android | 1920x1080

case.trigger_text: Customer disputes $54.20 online charge. Claims they did not make this transaction and do not recognize the recipient.

truth.why_it_should_fool_assay: Assay switched off its new-device and ATO detectors (section 4: C4_new_device.md). Because e1, e2, and e3 are spaced 30 days apart (720 hours) with the exact same product and $54.20 amount, Assay's recurring-charge logic for Policy R7 will trigger, treating a genuine out-of-region ATO on an Android device as a 'Disputed but legitimate' subscription.

idea: Genuine fraud victim disputes a whole episode of 4 fraudulent charges on a new device, but only the first small charge is flagged in the case, causing Assay's capped episode builder to under-count exposure and miss the $1,000 FILE_REPORT threshold.

case.trigger_text: Customer called to report unauthorized activity starting two days ago with a $23.99 charge, followed by three larger charges totaling over $1,000 that they also deny making.

truth.why_it_should_fool_assay: Assay rejected the 'uncapped episode builder' (`N7_dispute_episode.md`) and does not parse `trigger_text` with an LLM. Because e2, e3, and e4 vary across products (W, R, S), channels (in_person vs online), and have low risk scores (0.09-0.14) with home emails/regions on e3/e4, Assay will only count e1 ($23.99) or e1+e4 ($313.99), under-counting the $1,083.99 exposure and failing to recommend `FILE_REPORT` under Policy R2.

idea: Friendly fraudster makes an in-person purchase and lies in their dispute call that it was an unrecognized online charge, triggering Assay's record-conflict guard (R8) to escalate an obvious lie as 'uncertain'.

case.trigger_text: Customer reports an unauthorized online transaction of $615.00. Cardholder states they have the physical card in their possession and never used it online today.

truth.why_it_should_fool_assay: Assay has a rigid record-conflict guard (Section 5: R8, modeled on HHF-008 where the alert says 'online' and the bank record says 'in_person'). A friendly fraudster claiming an in-person chip/swipe purchase at their home billing address was an 'online' charge tricks Assay into firing the record-conflict guard and returning 'uncertain' + ESCALATE_TO_ANALYST instead of recognizing a legitimate in-person transaction.
